newsitem.title: UK: MFI may consider dropping upholstery range.
newsitem.headline: MFI may consider dropping upholstery range.

text.p: British furniture retailer MFI Furniture Group Plc said on Tuesday it was getting unsatisfactory returns from upholstery and might consider dropping it as a product range.
Chairman Derek Hunt told a news conference that MFI's upholstery was not making money and the group was looking at this situation as part of a review of the group's entire product range.

"I would prefer to think we could make a better job of it, but everything goes on the table," he said, adding that the new MFI Homeworks format had enabled the group to track more closely the performance of different products.

Large amounts of space were devoted to upholstery in the old-style MFI stores, but the new Homeworks format, which now makes up half the 186-store chain, has much less space given over to soft furnishings.
Hunt said the review was looking mainly at non-core products, which included anything outside kitchens, bedroom furniture and bedding.
He said a decision to get out of upholstery would not mean big stock write-offs. The upholstery range represented about three percent of sales, he added.
Earlier, MFI reported a 21-percent increase in profits for last year to 70.3 million stg.
